author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can narrow the veterinarian list to one specialty through the address
summary: Both veterinarian list surfaces, the paged directory page and the machine-readable list, accept an optional specialty name and list only the veterinarians holding that specialty. Whole-name, case-insensitive matching; without a name both behave as today.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-003] GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only veterinarians holding that specialty, and pagination applies to the filtered list (page count and items reflect the filtered set).
[REQ-VET-003] GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns a JSON document whose vet list holds only veterinarians holding that specialty.
[REQ-VET-003] Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive: 'RADIOLOGY' matches radiology; a prefix such as 'radio' matches no veterinarian. Applies to both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] A specialty name no veterinarian holds yields HTTP 200 with the normal page or JSON document and an empty vet list, on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] An empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves exactly as if the parameter were absent, on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] On a filtered directory spanning more than one page, every pagination link (numbered, first, previous, next, last) carries the same specialty parameter.
[REQ-VET-003] Without the specialty parameter, /vets.html and /vets behave as today: every veterinarian listed, the HTML page paged.
[REQ-VET-003] Edge case 2: a veterinarian holding several specialties appears once in a filtered list when one of them matches.
[REQ-VET-004] GET /vets returns every veterinarian with their specialties; the existing showResourcesVetList test carries this bullet.
non_goals: No form, dropdown, or other page control on either surface; the filter is a URL contract only (owner: a visible control may come as a follow-up request).
Free-text veterinarian search and filtering by veterinarian name (NG-9 keeps free-text search out; name filtering is an open question).
Search for pets or visits (NG-9 unchanged for them).
Pagination of the JSON endpoint; it stays unpaged as today.
Repeated specialty parameters and trimming of surrounding spaces around a non-blank value: left open in the PRD Open Questions, not part of this contract.
notes: Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions per the owner's instruction to take the narrowest reading: visible control (deferred by owner), surrounding spaces on a non-blank value, multiple specialty values, name filtering under narrowed NG-9. REQ-VET-004 is the fresh requirement for the reinstated JSON endpoint; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and unreused. NG-9 narrowing recorded in docs/adr/2026-10-25-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md; that ADR needs a row in docs/adr/README.md Index, outside this agent's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Extends the existing paged repository search seam (OwnerRepository/OwnerController paged prefix search, system-design.md § Contracts) to the vet package; no new type, module, or pattern. Adjustment: VetRepository gains paged and unpaged Specialty-narrowed queries that are deliberately uncached, with case folded inside the query so H2, MySQL and PostgreSQL agree (new ADR 2026-10-25-specialty-filter-queried-uncached). VetController normalizes a blank value to absent (binding, architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row) and delegates; the matching rule stays out of the controller. New § Scale and Load section with the two vet rows; Contracts rows for Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController now carry REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004; the 'machine-readable route serves no requirement' Known Defects row is removed since REQ-VET-004 reinstates the surface. Covering-code basis: grep and file reads of VetController, VetRepository, OwnerController (IDE oracle not connected; weaker basis).
integration_points: Binding: both /vets.html and /vets take the Specialty as an optional request-scoped String request parameter (no persisted type bound). Empty or whitespace-only becomes absent and takes the existing cached unfiltered path; a non-blank value is passed unchanged (trimming is a PRD open question; narrowest reading). The page parameter keeps its current binding.

Repository boundary (matching semantics): ClinicServiceTests exercises the new VetRepository queries against the real embedded H2 database with seed data. Whole-name match, case-insensitivity ('RADIOLOGY'), prefix non-match ('radio'), unknown name yields empty, a vet with several specialties appears once, and the paged total matches the filtered set are all asserted there, against the real implementation.

Repository boundary (web tests): VetControllerTests keeps its existing @MockitoBean VetRepository framework stub, because the web slice carries no JPA context. Stubs cover only what the controller decides: which query is called for absent, blank, and non-blank values; the empty-result 200 page and JSON; and page links carrying the parameter. No matching logic is re-asserted against the stub.

Framework transport: MockMvc drives the real MVC dispatch, binding, and Thymeleaf rendering, per testing-principles.md (normalization tested at the web level, line on rules the design doc assigns to the controller).

Template: every directory page link (numbered, first, previous, next, last) is built with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}. The specialty parameter is present only when a filter is active, so an unfiltered page renders no dangling parameter.

patterns.description: paged search: normalize the parameter in the controller, delegate to a paged repository query, reuse addPaginationModel
existing findPaginated helper and page size; the filtered path reuses it rather than declaring a second page size
query at the database, parameterized, lower-cased on both sides, no @Cacheable on filtered reads

risks.risk: Cache growth from caller-chosen keys: putting @Cacheable("vets") on the filtered queries turns arbitrary Specialty spellings into entries in an unbounded JCache cache (system-design.md § Scale and Load, Limits row; security-principles.md Trust Boundaries, privilege row).
risks.mitigation: Filtered queries carry no cache annotation; only the unfiltered reads stay cached (ADR 2026-10-25-specialty-filter-queried-uncached).

risks.risk: Vendor-divergent case matching, the same defect as PostgreSQL owner search (system-design.md § Known Defects).
risks.mitigation: Fold case inside the JPQL with lower() on both the column and the parameter; never rely on column collation or a derived IgnoreCase that depends on vendor typing.

risks.risk: Duplicate rows or a wrong page count from a join on specialties: the H2 and MySQL vet_specialties tables carry no uniqueness constraint, and Specialty names are not unique by case (PRD edge case 2).
risks.mitigation: Use select distinct with an explicit count(distinct) countQuery, or an exists subquery, so the content and the total agree. Give the filtered paged query a deterministic order (by id) so pages partition the filtered set.

risks.risk: Injection into data access (security-principles.md Realization, injection row).
risks.mitigation: An @Query with a named bind parameter only; no string concatenation of the Specialty value.

risks.risk: Template expression injection or XSS: the current links use __${...}__ preprocessing, which would evaluate a request-derived value as an expression (security-principles.md Realization, cross-site scripting row; system-design.md Threat Model).
risks.mitigation: Pass the Specialty only as a link-expression parameter, which Thymeleaf URL-encodes; never put it inside preprocessing or string-built hrefs.

risks.risk: Vet directory and filtered list paths scale with data (system-design.md § Scale and Load rows: unrecorded, treated as bounded).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: one parameterized query per request, plus a count for the directory; no in-memory filtering.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to audit. Added the Index rows for the product expert's non-goal ADR 2026-10-25-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md and for the new ADR. system-design.md gained a § Scale and Load section (it was missing) and two Threat Model rows (cache growth, template expression injection); the SQL-injection row now says 'parameterized JPQL queries'. The REQ-VET-004 bullet is carried by the existing showResourcesVetList test; the JSON endpoint stays unpaged. Out of scope: trimming a non-blank value, multiple specialty values, name filtering (PRD Open Questions).

findings.description: The test cannot fail under the change it exists to catch. author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: both new VetRepository queries bind the request-derived name as a named JPQL parameter (`lower(s.name) = lower(:specialty)` with `@Param("specialty")`, VetRepository.java in the diff); no query text is concatenated from request input, meeting the security-principles Injection row.

Template expression injection: the specialty reaches vetList.html only as a link-expression parameter (`@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`), which Thymeleaf URL-encodes and th:href attribute-escapes; `grep -rn -F '__${' src/main/resources/templates/` returns no vetList.html line, so the change also removed the page-number preprocessing that template previously used. The test asserting `/vets.html?page=1&specialty=radiology` exercises the encoded output.

XSS: the specialty is never rendered as text in vetList.html and is not echoed in the /vets JSON body (Vets carries only the repository result); no th:utext was introduced (`grep -rn -F 'utext' src/main/resources/templates/` returns nothing).

Cache-growth DoS: both filtered reads are deliberately uncached (no @Cacheable on findAllBySpecialtyName, javadoc and ADR state why), so caller-chosen names cannot grow the unbounded vet cache; the existing @Cacheable("vets") reads keep their fixed keys.

Exposed surface: no new endpoint; the optional `specialty` @RequestParam on the two existing GET routes is a read-only narrowing of data both routes already return in full. No request-bound object, no @ModelAttribute/@RequestBody, no binder change; no check, annotation, or escaping call was removed.

Error handling: a blank or absent specialty falls back to the unfiltered read; an unmatched name yields an empty list, not an exception, so no new exception message reaches the error page. The pre-existing page<1 IllegalArgumentException path is unchanged by this slice.
Secrets and logging: the diff adds no credential, token, or log statement; no Runtime/ProcessBuilder, file I/O, or deserialization was introduced.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set and no dependency changed. OWASP dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (`grep -n -F 'dependencyCheck' build.gradle` returns nothing), so no NVD match ran in this review; resolved runtimeClasspath shows Spring Boot 4.1.1 (spring-boot-thymeleaf), spring-webmvc 7.0.9, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, jackson-databind 3.1.5, hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: The query-parameter escaping in vetList.html:27 is now done by hand rather than by the link-expression parameter syntax, so it relies on the `#uris.escapeQueryParam` call staying in place. The only link-carrying test (VetControllerTests.java:195 `/vets.html?page=1&specialty=radiology`) uses a value with no reserved characters. approved_aspects: Fix-delta scope (changeset.py --base-tree e742afd1b75ea4d638eb0629a415730d427d2ce7 --name-only): docs/prd.md, docs/system-design.md, vetList.html and two test files. Only vetList.html is production surface. VetController.java and VetRepository.java are unchanged since my line-16 approval, so the parameterized JPQL binding approved there still holds.

Pagination-link escaping in vetList.html: the link-expression parameter `specialty=${specialty}` was replaced by an explicitly escaped suffix. vetList.html:27 reads `th:with="narrowing=${specialty != null} ? The request-derived value is still query-parameter escaped, using Thymeleaf's own URI utility, so `&`, `=`, `#`, quotes and angle brackets cannot add parameters or break the URL. th:href then HTML-escapes the attribute value. Neighboring pagination in ownersList.html (for example line 35 `th:href="@{'/owners?page=' + ${i}}"`) concatenates only integer page numbers, so no other template carries a request-derived string in a query, and no competing escaping convention exists for this one to diverge from.

author: change-grader
summary: filter both vet list routes by specialty

blast_radius.note: Production edits stay in the vet package (VetController, VetRepository, vetList.html) plus two test files and slice docs; no sensitive paths, no build or config change, and the 50 hunks are mostly PRD and system-design prose.
